[Reading notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_hMHTmUAKbZox1Kcbe5CMEzsABAGuJ7B8CJW1_4EweM/edit)
in Google Docs.

James Hollis is a Jungian analyst, and his subject is the second half of life
as its own developmental task rather than a decline from the first. The identity
assembled in the first half, built to meet the demands of family and career,
stops answering in the second, and what replaces it has to be chosen
deliberately. The book sits close to
[the puer aeternus notes](puer-aeternus.qmd), which describe the failure to
make that passage at all.
